hook.text: In Mina, you never missed Fajr. Since then: 4 out of 180.

verses.text: “They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness.”

end.text: In Mina, you never missed Fajr. Why here?
end.gold: Tonight: one alarm. Phone across the room. Fajr.

captions: Mina. 4:50 a.m. Three million people, already awake.
Nobody needed an alarm. The whole valley stood up.
You cried in sujood. You promised: “Never again.”
Six months later. Your room. 6:58 a.m.
Fajr was at 6:41. The alarm: snoozed. Twice.
Then your lock screen. You, in white. Mina at dawn.
That man would never have slept through this.
The next night: one alarm. 6:20. Phone across the room.
Cold water. Your hands still remember.
No three million. Just you, and four old men.

post.caption:
In Mina, you never missed Fajr. Since then: 4 out of 180. 🤍

Mina, 4:50 a.m. Three million people awake without an alarm. You cried in sujood and promised: never again. Six months later: 6:58 a.m., the alarm snoozed twice — and on your lock screen, you in white, Mina at dawn.

“They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness.” (51:17-18)

Tonight: one alarm. Phone across the room. Fajr.
